chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd alman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot a prayer until the time for another prayer entered. He said: When he forgets the prayer or sleeps through it, he prays when he remembers it. So when he remembers it while he is in a prayer, he begins with that which he forgot. And if he remembers it with an Imam during the Maghrib prayer, he completes it with one Rak'ah, then prays Maghrib, then prays Al-'Atamah (Isha) after it. And if he had prayed Al-'Atamah alone, so he prayed two Rak'at from it, then remembers that he forgot Maghrib, he completes it with one Rak'ah, so the Maghrib prayer becomes three Rak'at. Then he prays Al-'Atamah after that.
ai.seo_question: How to make up a missed prayer if remembered during another prayer time?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the Shia jurisprudential principle that missed obligatory prayers due to sleep or forgetfulness are made up individually (Qada) without requiring repetition of the current prayer, emphasizing the continuity of worship. It provides specific procedural details for integrating missed Maghrib and Isha prayers, reflecting the practical application of divine mercy in maintaining the daily ritual structure. The ruling underscores the Shia view that the obligation to perform the prayer remains even if the prescribed time has passed, provided it is performed before the next prayer's time expires.
